patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header should remain accessible during scroll without obscuring content; if implemented as fixed/sticky it needs proper offset handling across mobile and desktop.

patterns_found.behavior_notes: A menu button should toggle the primary navigation open/closed, likely as an overlay or expandable panel beneath the header.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The hamburger icon itself is not explicitly drawn; this is inferred from the responsive difference between mobile and desktop header density.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The inferred mobile menu toggle/panel and any sticky header interactions require keyboard-operable state changes and managed focus; desktop navigation also needs logical focus handling because it contains multiple interactive links in the header.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move into the menu and return to the trigger on close; keyboard navigation through header controls should remain logical across breakpoints.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly static article/detail page with low JavaScript complexity. The main cross-viewport interaction difference is navigation: desktop appears to have room for exposed nav links, while mobile likely needs a collapsed menu. Aside from that, the page reads as content-forward with a CTA button and related-content/sidebar blocks that do not by themselves imply advanced JS behaviors such as tabs, accordions, modals, search, or dynamic loading.
